about.title: About this site
about.intro: This is a free, non-commercial Islamic resource. No ads, no tracking, no accounts required, no paywalls.
about.whyBody: There are many Islamic apps, and yet most sell data, run ads, or lock features behind paywalls. This site is a small attempt at something different: everything free, everything sourced, nothing tracked.
about.howBody: Quran text comes from Tanzil. Translations come from published, licensed translators. Hadith come from Sunnah.com with authenticity grading. Duas come from Hisnul Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim), each with a source reference. Anything without a source doesn't get published.
about.notABody: It is not a fatwa engine. It is not a substitute for a qualified scholar. For religious rulings, please consult a local imam or an established Q&A resource — the sources page links several.

faq.q1: What is a dua in Islam?
faq.a1: A duʿāʾ (دُعَاء) is a personal supplication or invocation to Allah — distinct from ṣalāh (the formal five daily prayers). Duas can be recited in any language and at any time, though the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ taught many specific duas for specific moments.
faq.q2: Where do the duas on this site come from?
faq.a2: Every dua on this site is from a classical source — the Ṣaḥīḥayn (Bukhārī and Muslim), the four Sunan (Abū Dāwūd, at-Tirmidhī, an-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah), or directly from the Quran itself. The exact hadith number is cited on each entry.
faq.q3: Do I have to say the dua in Arabic?
faq.a3: No. Duas may be said in any language. The Arabic text is provided for those learning or memorizing the Prophetic wording; transliteration helps with pronunciation; the translation preserves the meaning.

account.pageDescription: Sign in to sync your bookmarks, notes, memorization deck and settings across devices. No email required. No tracking.
account.syncActiveBody: Your bookmarks, notes, memorization deck and settings sync automatically to any device where you sign in with this username. Changes replicate within a few seconds.
account.passphraseHelpSignUp: At least 12 characters. Write it down — there is no reset.
account.passphraseHelpSignIn: The passphrase you set when you created the account.
account.noRecoveryBody: We don't collect email, so we can't send you a reset link. If you forget your passphrase, the account is lost. Save your passphrase in a password manager.
account.faqDataA: Your Quran bookmarks, personal notes, memorization deck, fasting log, prayer streak, dhikr counts, and settings — everything under iw.v1 in your browser.
account.faqEmailA: Because we don't want to. No email means no spam, no marketing lists, no data breaches. The trade-off is you can't reset a forgotten passphrase.
account.faqDeleteQ: How do I delete my account?
account.faqDeleteA: Sign in, go to Settings, and use "Delete my data". That wipes your device and the server copy. Anyone wanting a proper account-delete endpoint should ask — we'll add it.
account.errorUsernameTaken: That username is already taken. Try another.
account.errorPassphraseShort: Passphrase must be at least 12 characters.
account.errorUsernameShape: Username can only contain letters, digits, underscore, and hyphen (3-64 chars).

page.title: Install as an app
page.description: This site works as a Progressive Web App — install it to your device and you get the same experience as a native app, without the App Store review, tracking, or 50 MB download.
page.featureOfflineBody: Quran text, du'a collection, prayer time schedule and Salah tutorials are cached — usable on a flight or in a low-signal area.
page.featureHomeBody: Launches in its own window with no browser chrome. Feels like a native app, tapped from the same place.
page.featureFastBody: Second visits load instantly. No app-store update cycle — improvements ship the moment we push them.
page.iosStep1: Open this page in Safari (Chrome for iOS can't install PWAs — Apple limitation).
page.iosStep2: Tap the Share button (the square with an arrow pointing up).
page.iosStep3: Scroll down and tap 'Add to Home Screen'.
page.iosStep4: Tap 'Add' in the top-right. The Islamic Website icon appears on your home screen.
page.androidStep1: Open the menu (three dots, top right).
page.androidStep2: Tap 'Install app' or 'Add to Home screen'.
page.androidStep3: Confirm. The app icon appears in your app drawer.
page.desktopBody: Look for the install icon in the address bar (a small screen with a down-arrow). Click it, then 'Install'. The site opens in its own window and gets a Start menu / Dock entry.
page.nativeQuestion: Is there an iOS/Android app in the App Store?
page.nativeAnswer: No — and by design. A native app means store review cycles, forced updates, and 50 MB downloads for what is fundamentally a text-and-audio website. The PWA gives you everything a native app would (offline, home screen icon, fullscreen, notifications) without any of the cost. If you already installed via 'Add to Home Screen', you already have the app.
